entertainment.title: Does Georgia Still Want to Be the Hollywood of the South?
entertainment.summary: At a time when the fight for productions is fierce, new governor Keisha Lance Bottoms faces a major question - and challenge.
entertainment.body:
A few years ago, if you wanted to shoot a movie in Georgia, you’d better have made your reservations early.

The lack of an annual cap on credit payouts, the solid 30 percent rebate, the allowance of (some) above-the-line expenses, and the lower cost of housing compared with New York and California made it so that every inch of the state’s 21st century studio space and hotel inventory could get booked up.

MacGyver , Ozark , Stranger Things , The Resident and nearly every significant Marvel TV and film project were all among those calling Georgia home even when many of their stories were set elsewhere. And then there was Tyler Perry’s Fort McPherson studio and its 50,000 square feet of permanent sets, which opened in 2019 and housed numerous projects. The state’s film and TV growth was astronomical — over barely a dozen years beginning in 2010, studio square footage went from 45,000 all the way to 3 million.

But while Perry continues to book productions at his landmark location, Hollywood activity has thinned markedly in the Peach State since 2022. The Georgia Film Office reports that production spend has cratered from a peak of $4.4 billion in 2022 to $2.3 billion in 2025 — hardly peanuts ( Will Trent , The Rock’s Lizard Music and Judd Apatow’s The Comeback King have been among recent shoots) but a major fall. Total productions saw a similar drop, from 412 to 245.

And the numbers continue to sink. Industry tracker ProdPro says that Georgia saw about $1.56 billion in film and TV production spend in the 12 months ending in September, down 15 percent from $1.84 billion in the prior 12-month period.

There have been other worrisome developments. Lee Thomas, longtime head of the Georgia Film Office and the major force behind the surge, announced her retirement this summer. Her replacement has not been named. And then in early November, another blow: James Gunn, who famously loved Georgia and brought DC projects like Peacemaker and Superman to the sprawling Trillith Studios in Fayetteville, was ousted as head of the superhero division under new Skydance ownership.

Gunn’s love affair with Georgia runs deep; he shot the first two Guardians of the Galaxy movies for Marvel and even owned a home there. The director’s big-budget Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow alone, which shot in the state this summer, gave Georgia its best production spend quarter for new shoots since early 2024, ProdPro notes. But his successor, Jeremy Latcham, and Latcham’s boss, David Ellison, could shop for preferred alternatives with less allegiance to the past.

entertainment.title: Santa Barbara Film Fest: Penélope Cruz Set for Arlington Artist of the Year Award (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: The Oscar winner is having a banner year highlighted by standout performances in 'Bunker,' 'The Invite' and 'La Bola Negra.'
entertainment.body:
Penélope Cruz, the Oscar-winning actress whose 2026 credits include the Sundance sensation The Invite , Toronto audience award winner La Bola Negra and forthcoming Bunker , has been tapped by the Santa Barbara International Film Festival to receive its Arlington Artist of the Year Award, The Hollywood Reporter can exclusively report.

Cruz, the most celebrated Spanish film actress of all time and one of only a handful of Europeans who have become bona fide A-list stars in Hollywood, will collect her award at Santa Barbara’s historic Arlington Theatre on Thursday, Feb. 11, 2027. It will be presented to her by a special guest at the end of an evening of clips and conversation about her entire career, which will be moderated by SBIFF fest executive director Roger Durling. Related Stories Movies IDA Documentary Awards Nominations: 'Concrete Land,' 'To Hold a Mountain,' 'You Can See Everything' Among Top Nominees Movies 'The Odyssey' to Receive Ensemble Performance Award at Palm Springs International Film Festival (Exclusive)

“Over the past three decades, Penélope has evolved into one of cinema’s most surprising and revelatory performers,” Durling tells THR . “Witnessing her growth as an artist, and the depth and maturity she has brought to each new role, has been nothing short of extraordinary.”

Over the 34 years since Cruz’s big screen debut in the Spanish film Jamon, Jamon opposite Javier Bardem, who is now her husband, she has consistently done extraordinary work on both sides of the Atlantic. She is probably best known, though, for her seven collaborations with the great Spanish auteur Pedro Almodóvar: 1997’s Live Flesh , 1999’s All About My Mother , 2006’s Volver , 2009’s Broken Embraces , 2013’s I’m So Excited! , 2019’s Pain and Glory and 2021’s Parallel Mothers .

The only person who has won at least one acting award from each of the five most prominent European film academies, she also has starred in two films that won the best international feature Oscar (1992’s Belle Epoque and All About My Mother ), became the first Spanish actress ever to be nominated for an acting Oscar (for Volver ), subsequently received three additional acting Oscar noms (for 2008’s Vicky Cristina Barcelona , 2009’s Nine and Parallel Mothers ), and became, in 2009, the first — and, to this day, only — Spanish actress to win an acting Oscar (for Vicky Cristina Barcelona ).

But never has Cruz had a single year quite like 2026, in which she has given three great performances: as a bohemian sexologist Olivia Wilde’s The Invite (A24); as a bawdy cabaret singer entertaining troops during the Spanish Civil War in Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo’s La Bola Negra (Netflix); and as a book editor enduring marital strife in Florian Zeller’s Bunker (Sony Classics).

Glen Powell is a country star whose career hits a sour note in the trailer for filmmaker Judd Apatow ‘s forthcoming comedy The Comeback King .

Apatow helmed the feature that Universal Pictures is set to release theatrically on Feb. 5, 2027. Cristin Milioti , Madelyn Cline , Stavros Halkias, Li Jin Hao and Kumail Nanjiani round out the cast.

The Comeback King centers on Powell as Aubrey King, a country star whose reputation changes after a false rumor that he cheated on his pop-star girlfriend (Cline). To restore his reputation, King sets out on a road to redemption that requires him to step out of the spotlight and finally earn his college degree. “I’m looking for a comeback here,” Powell admits in the trailer. “I got real things on my heart. I got real things that I want to sing.”

Powell, who teamed up with Apatow to pen the script, trained in guitar and vocals to perform several original songs from top songwriters in the genre. The Comeback King features performances from such real-life country performers as Jelly Roll, Brad Paisley, Miranda Lambert, Shaboozey, Chris Stapleton, Brandi Carlile, Luke Bryan and Reba McEntire.

entertainment.title: Your Favorite Coffee Shop Is Probably Streaming Music Illegally. It’s the Music Industry’s Fault, Too (Guest Column)
entertainment.summary: A new study found 81% of U.S. businesses don't properly license music, costing creators and other rightsholders. The fix starts with education — not lawsuits.
entertainment.body:
Walk into almost any shop, gym, salon or restaurant in America, and you’ll hear music. Ask the owner whether it’s licensed and you will likely get a confident “yes.” But in most cases, that answer is, unfortunately, wrong.

Soundtrack recently surveyed 1,525 decision-makers responsible for nearly 15,000 business locations across 10 customer-facing industries to find out how U.S. businesses actually play music. Though the law is clear that businesses need specific licenses to play music in public, the results of the survey describe a market that loves music, depends on it, and, overwhelmingly, does not properly pay for it.

Ninety-seven percent of the businesses we surveyed play music for customers, and 77% do it every day. Adjusted for the size of the U.S., that means roughly 3.8 million U.S. business locations play music in their stores.

Nine in 10 of those surveyed said music boosts employee motivation and shapes the energy of their space, while more than eight in 10 called it an essential part of the business and said it has to fit their brand. Rather than merely being a background expense, businesses see music as part of the product.

Yet despite this overwhelming demand, the way music played in businesses is paid for has not evolved. A striking 79% of businesses illicitly use a consumer streaming service, such as a personal Spotify, Pandora or YouTube account, to play music for customers. Only 28% of businesses use a service built and licensed for business. This is one of the biggest failures, and also one of the biggest opportunities, for the music industry today.

Aside from the scale of misuse, it is significant how many businesses are sure they’re doing it right. Seventy-eight percent of respondents were confident the music in their business is legally compliant. Eighty-three percent said they’re familiar with the rules. Yet 81% are misusing music, and 58% believe it’s legal to stream a personal account in their business.

Even I struggle to distill the U.S. licensing rules into just a few sentences; such is the unnecessary complexity surrounding them. Put simply, businesses require both a music service licensed for commercial use and licenses with all four U.S. performing rights organizations (PROs) — ASCAP, BMI, SESAC and GMR — that cover the music they play.

Some licensed music services bundle performance rights, while others require businesses to secure separate public performance licenses from U.S. PROs. For a business owner, working out exactly what’s included can be a job in itself.

entertainment.title: Will ‘GTA 6’ Crash PlayStation and Xbox Tonight? Oddsmakers Are Betting On It
entertainment.summary: PlayStation, Xbox and internet providers are bracing: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' might literally break the internet.
entertainment.body:
Will the recent outage apocalypse also strike the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI ?

As of Wednesday morning, a major online betting site, BetOnline , says there’s an implied 83 percent chance of a PlayStation or Xbox outage after the highly anticipated game is launched at midnight.

Which makes sense. The last week has seen disruptions affect Microsoft, Apple, airlines, banks, the FAA and even the NSA. With everything going down lately, does anyone really think the biggest game launch in history will go smoothly? Related Stories Business 'Grand Theft Auto 6' Reviews: "I Never Want to Leave" Business 'GTA 6' vs. Hollywood: Industry Braces for "Biggest Entertainment Launch in History"

PlayStation and Xbox have been doing what they can to try and limit disruption. Both companies have urged players to pre-download the roughly 212GB game, which is the most pre-ordered title in PlayStation Store and Microsoft Store history (“Given this unprecedented demand, we’ve joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they’re ready to play on launch day,” PlayStation said in a statement).

Once the single-player game is downloaded, a player should be able to play offline without making further demands on the console companies’ servers.

But this assumes the vast majority of players have planned in advance and don’t wait until the day of release to get the game — and how likely does that sound? While hardcore gamers have likely been locked and loaded for days, GTA 6 will almost certainly draw legions of casual players reading the game’s positive reviews and media hype. Plus activities like players activating the game, signing into PlayStation accounts, and playing via cloud streaming could cause disruption.

Other potential choke points are internet service providers. Comcast says GTA 6 ‘s first 48 hours of pre-downloads constituted the largest single event in its network history. The company further predicted that Nov. 19 will its busiest internet traffic day ever. “We’re about to break all-time highs,” Comcast chief network officer Elad Nafshi told Inc .

Surprisingly, for those hoping to play the game who haven’t yet upgraded to a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S, you’re in luck. The consoles are currently listed as in stock at major U.S. retailers like Target, Walmart and Best Buy. This might not last, however. The Game Business previously reported that at least one major retailer is expecting the consoles to sell out ahead of the holidays. “We’ve been informed that because of the on-going issues around hardware component availability, we won’t be getting the units we want ahead of [ GTA 6 ],” the source said. “Demand will likely outstrip supply during the year end period”). So if you want to return to Vice City, you better buy a console before you have to steal it.

entertainment.title: Grimes & Elon Musk Feud Over AI ‘Sex Slave,’ Singer Urges Ex to ‘Step Up’ and Be ‘the King He Used to Be’

entertainment.body:
Grimes and Elon Musk are just like any pair of exes with lingering disagreements. They just so happen to be hashing them out on a social media platform that one of them owns, and the root of their conflict just so happens to be about controversial technology that the musician’s former partner has plans to invest billions in.

In a series of back-and-forth posts on X (which Musk has owned since 2022) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), Grimes and the billionaire tech entrepreneur — who share three children — butted heads over Claudia, a new “influencer” fully generated by artificial intelligence . After Musk reposted a video of Claudia with the endorsement, “Super intelligence will hack your limbic system,” the Canadian artist directly replied to him, writing, “The fixation on fake women feels like cope.”

“I’m a fan of Claudia, but … she isn’t a she, shes an alien creature who’s both blessed and haunted by the entirety of ancestral memory,” Grimes continued. “Secualizing a species that cannot have sex is the ultimate definition of Nietzsche’s last man, and we can do better than reducing ‘it’ to a sex slave.”

Musk replied to this with “Take the White Pill,” alongside which he also shared a video of Claudia “singing” a song about how AI is destined to help humans live better lives.

But Grimes doesn’t seem like she’s taking the “white pill” any time soon. To one commenter who’d pushed back on her initial comment by asserting that “Most men don’t read Nietzsche,” the electro-pop musician tagged Musk and wrote: “Our leaders should read Nietzsche and Elon has read Nietzsche … He’s an unelected king. He could and should step into the role and confront his responsibility to society, if he wanted to.”

She went on to say that her ex “can do better” and should “rise above it,” adding, “He shud be the king we all wish he was. The king he used to be. Ima stop saying this in private and say it online. If he wud step up and be magnanimous he could earn the Mandate of Heaven – which currently he has lost.”

Musk jumped in on this thread as well, clapping back w ith , “I don’t want to be king and Starship has the Mandate of Heaven,” referencing his reusable SpaceX spacecraft.

In more replies to other commenters on the topic, Grimes also wrote of Musk: “a man who worries so publicly abt the birth rate should not publicly advocate for its demise” as well as “If Elon respected women in public the whole world cud change.”

Originally from New York, the Puerto Rican actress has built up a string of television credits, appearing in series such as “Blindspot,” “The Blacklist,” “Jessica Jones” and “Chicago P.D.,” per IMDb .

entertainment.title: Bruce Dickinson Already Has a New Solo Album and Tour Dates on Deck for Iron Maiden’s Break
entertainment.summary: Hard-working hard rocker will release PsychoGod , which he's teasing with "Speaking in Tongues," this winter
entertainment.body:
Bruce Dickinson must be determined to be the hardest-working man in hard rock and metal. He’s currently on tour in Australia with Iron Maiden — frankly too busy to attend the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, which inducted Maiden on Saturday — but here he is announcing a new solo album, PsychoGod , with a cinematic music video that doubles as an allegory about the prison industrial complex for the single “Speaking in Tongues.” The album will come out March 12, and he has solo tour dates scheduled all around Europe in between Iron Maiden’s North American trek . And it’s only been two years since Dickinson released his last solo album, The Mandrake Project .

Dickinson sings the PsychoGod song “Speaking in Tongues” with his trademark urgency. Its intro recalls Maiden’s “Fear of the Dark,” but it soon becomes a unique plea for understanding all leading to the revelation: “Tell the truth, and the world will know just what you mean.”

“‘Speaking in tongues’ is an expression used to describe a form of religious or sacred ecstasy in which celebrants often lose control of normal speech and bodily functions,” Dickinson said in a statement. “Their search for truth at the expense of sanity contrasts sharply with the shallow world of the Internet, social media and the narcissist political classes that seem to dominate our lives.”

The video, which Dickinson co-directed with Leo Liberti, shows the singer both shouting at the heavens in a Nevada desert as his band plays and under arrest in orange prison gear as he’s accused of trafficking drugs in L.A. There are cartoons of people wagging their tongues (including tongue-touching nuns) all as bigwigs laugh at his misfortune.

Dickinson said in a statement that the video is the first of five interconnected stories, “a karmic journey” connected by the album’s songs. “As a first video, ‘Speaking in Tongues’ is brutal, violent and [it] holds a mirror to the ugly global world of accusation, incarceration, conspiracy, and lies. Each subsequent video is a movie in its own right but, like a jigsaw puzzle, the pieces will drop into place as the journey continues.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Dickinson and his band recorded the album live at Dave Grohl’s Studio 606 with a guest list that includes Devin Townsend and Sepultura’s Andreas Kisser and Derrick Green. Grohl, Slash, and members of Anthrax and Angra all stopped by the sessions as well.

entertainment.title: The Rings Of Power: Sauron's Motivations In The Lord Of The Rings Series Explained
entertainment.summary: What does Sauron really want to accomplish in Middle-earth? Here's what's behind his plans in The Rings of Power and how he compares to his predecessor.
entertainment.body:
Ben Rothstein/Prime Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 6 — "From Valinor"

"The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 5 opens with Sauron (Charlie Vickers) talking about finding "a secret so precious, it will shape the fortunes of all." Then he starts waxing on about the mighty hour coming, final victories, and an age of peace. Amid the trauma bonding of Season 3, Episode 6 , Sauron revisits his plans when he interrogates Celeborn (Jamie Campbell Bower) about forging Elven Rings of Power. Celeborn asks him why he's doing this. Sauron's chilling response? "It will bring me bliss." The Dark Lord monologues about the true joy of his existence: to feel the never-ending moment of others submitting to his will.

With all this talk about rings, domination, and blissful subservience, it begs the question, what on Middle-earth is Sauron trying to accomplish here? Is he really just trying to get his jollies from controlling others? In short, yes, Sauron is the ultimate control freak. Practically speaking, his plans boil down to infusing magical rings with his own power so he can dominate the will of others. (That's how he turns powerful, stubborn Men into Ringwraiths , for instance.)

But don't let "I do this for bliss" make you think Sauron's just controlling people for the fun of it. His ring-based power plan is actually deeply inspired by a part of his identity that goes back to before his original fall. Before Sauron controlled others for his own nefarious purposes, his strength was bringing order and control to Arda (the name for God's green Earth in Tolkien's legendarium).

Prime Video In the book "Morgoth's Ring," Tolkien explains, "It had been [Sauron's] virtue (and therefore also the cause of his fall, and of his relapse) that he loved order and coordination, and disliked all confusion and wasteful friction." It elaborates that Sauron's original virtue was in loving and understanding other beings. It's only over time that this translates into control issues. This is distinctly different from the disposition of Sauron's original master, the Dark Lord Morgoth.

Morgoth is purely a corrupting force. "Morgoth's Ring" says, "To gain domination over Arda, Morgoth had let most of his being pass into the physical constituents of the Earth." This gives the original Dark Lord influence over creation itself. It goes on to explain that Morgoth was self-obsessed and a sower of discord. He hated the will of others, and "his sole ultimate object was their destruction."

entertainment.title: Warner Bros. TV, Paramount TV Studios to Combine as a Single Mega-Studio
entertainment.summary: Channing Dungey and Matt Thunell will lead the combined studio, while CBS Studios remains separate under David Stapf.
entertainment.body:
Skydance is making a big move with its TV studios, combining Warner Bros. Television and Paramount Television Studios into a single entity that will have more than 100 productions under its umbrella.

The combined studio will be known as Warner Bros. Television Studios, a nod to the larger of the two current units. The new organization will officially launch early next year, with each group operating as usual until then. WBTV chief Channing Dungey and PTVS head Matt Thunell will be presidents of the combined studio, reporting to Skydance TV co-chair and chief content officer George Cheeks. Dungey also continues to lead Skydance’s cable portfolio.

CBS Studios , headed by David Stapf , will keep operating as its own entity. CBS Studios International, Skydance Sports Entertainment and nonfiction unit See It Now Studios fall under CBS Studios. BET Studios will become part of Warner Bros. TV Studios.

“Bringing together two of the industry’s most prolific television studios creates a formidable creative engine, uniting extraordinary talent, resources, acclaimed programming and iconic franchises with the global scale to compete at the highest level,” Cheeks said in a statement. “With Channing and Matt at the helm, we have two exceptional leaders who understand what it takes to empower creative talent, foster bold ideas and deliver programming that resonates with audiences everywhere. Alongside CBS Studios, led by the incomparable David Stapf, Warner Bros. Television Studios gives us two world-class studios, with the breadth, depth and creative ambition to deliver for Skydance platforms and third-party partners across the industry.”

Dungey and Thunell — who previously worked together at Netflix — offered praise for their soon-to-be partnership in statements of their own.

“Matt has extraordinary creative instincts, and a deep understanding of great storytelling. I couldn’t ask for a better partner as we bring these storied studios together,” said Dungey. “We have a unique opportunity to create something truly special for our creative partners and audiences around the world. I’m very excited to begin this new chapter.”

Added Thunell, “Channing is one of the most accomplished and respected executives in our industry, with an extraordinary track record of building successful businesses, developing enduring partnerships and delivering some of television’s most acclaimed programming. Ever since our time together at Netflix, I’ve hoped we’d have the opportunity to work together again, and I’m thrilled that day has finally come.”

entertainment.title: The Sound of Rocky: How an Anthem Was Born
entertainment.summary: How a 90-second musical cue for a low-budget boxing movie became an enduring anthem of perseverance inspiring generations far beyond the big screen.
entertainment.body:
When composer Bill Conti first sat down to write the music for Rocky ’s now-iconic training montage, he wasn’t trying to create one of the most recognizable anthems in cinematic history.

Director John G. Avildsen simply needed 90 seconds of music to accompany Sylvester Stallone’s transformation from a struggling Philadelphia boxer into a legitimate heavyweight contender.

Conti took a melancholy theme he’d already developed for the film, gave it a more energetic tempo, and recorded a rough version for Avildsen to use in the editing room. Related Stories Movies How Rocky Became the Heart of Philadelphia Movies The Underdog Story Behind the Underdog Story

“He says, ‘I got five miles of film here. Give me another 30 seconds,’” Conti recalled. “I didn’t sit down to write a song. He needed a minute and a half. Then it grew to two, then two and a half and three.”

That unlikely creative process would eventually produce “Gonna Fly Now,” the triumphant theme that has accompanied Rocky Balboa ’s ascent up the Philadelphia Museum of Art steps for half a century.

Like the film itself, the music was created with limited resources and even less room for error.

Conti had joined the production through editor Richard Halsey and Avildsen, accepting a $25,000 all-inclusive arrangement to compose and record the film’s score.

“A package deal means exactly what it says,” Conti said. “You pay for everything, and you get what’s left.”

entertainment.title: ‘I Love Rock ‘n Roll’ Turns 45: An Oral History From Joan Jett, Kenny Laguna & More
entertainment.summary: "When it hit No. 1, the first thing I wanted to see was Billboard . I wanted to look at those charts," Jett shares of the iconic hit.
entertainment.body:
Joan Jett loved rock ‘n’ roll from the time she was an adolescent and swore to play it — especially after her first guitar teacher told her that “girls don’t play rock ‘n’ roll” and taught her “On Top of Old Smokey” instead. Explore Joan Jett Joan Jett & the Blackhearts See latest videos, charts and news

Born Joan Larkin in suburban Philadelphia, she started playing guitar in Rockville, Md., and really pursued her passion after her family moved to Los Angeles County. She began haunting Rodney Bingenheimer’s English Disco and co-founded The Runaways with drummer Sandy West and producer/impresario Kim Fowley in 1975. Related Noah Kahan Reacts to 2027 Grammy Nominations Snub: 'I Was In My Feelings for a Sec' 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Revs Its Engines & Leads 2026 Game Awards Nominations: Full List Cody Johnson on Why He's Skipping 2026 CMA Awards: 'Going 100 MPH All the Time Isn't Healthy'

“She was a Suzi Quatro fan,” remembers latter-day Runaways and Jett manager Toby Mamis, now of Alive Enterprises, who met Jett when he was working with Quatro. “She planted herself in the hotel lobby, too shy to introduce herself or ask for an autograph. But we looked at her, this girl that dressed like Suzi … and I would encourage her. I thought that a great outlet for her devotion to Suzi was playing rock ‘n’ roll the way Suzi did, being inspired by Elvis.”

The Runaways lasted four studio albums, charting a couple of singles (“Cherry Bomb,” “Heartbeat”) on the Bubbling Under Hot 100 chart and making more noise in Japan than anywhere else. (The sordid story, including Foley’s abuse, is chronicled in the 2004 documentary Edgeplay: A Film About the Runaways and in the 2010 biopic The Runaways .)

The band’s dissolution during the spring 1979 left Jett moribund for a time, but after dealing with some health issues, she launched a solo career. Mamis recruited pop writer-producers Kenny Laguna and Ritchie Cordell, who first worked with Jett on We’re All Crazee Now! (a never-finished film based on the Runaways), and then on her first album in 1980, known as Joan Jett in Europe and Bad Reputation the following year, after Jett signed with Neil Bogart’s Boardwalk Records in the U.S.

Produced by Laguna and Cordell, with two tracks by Sex Pistols’ Steve Jones and Paul Cook, the album was an auspicious start for Jett — who herself had produced albums for several bands, including the Germs, around that time. Combining originals and covers, Bad Reputation reached No. 51 on the Billboard 200, while the title track and a rendition of Gary Glitter’s “Do You Wanna Touch Me (Oh Yeah)” and Lesley Gore’s “You Don’t Own Me” received a modicum of radio attention.

Asked whether the equity injection is the start of a larger relationship with Musk, Ellison said he’d be “thrilled” to “collaborate with him in the future” when the right opportunity arises.

The investment has prompted speculation that Musk could look to interfere with CNN and CBS News, though Ellison said he’d defend the editorial independence of the publications.

“Our belief is truth-based, fact-based, bipartisan, down the middle, and, you know, present both sides of the argument and fundamentally let the audience decide what is right for them,” he said.

entertainment.title: How Rocky Became the Heart of Philadelphia
entertainment.summary: Fifty years after Rocky brought the City of Brotherly Love to the big screen, the fictional boxer’s working-class spirit remains inseparable from the city that shaped him.
entertainment.body:
Every year, visitors from around the world make the pilgrimage to the Philadelphia Museum of Art , where 72 stone steps have become one of cinema’s most recognizable landmarks. Many come not for artwork, but to recreate Rocky Balboa’s triumphant ascent, arms raised above the city that made him a legend.

But when Sylvester Stallone first raced up those steps in 1976, Philadelphia was a far cry from the tourist destination immortalized on screen.

At the time, the city was struggling economically, with its aging neighborhoods and industrial character reflecting the hardships faced by many of its residents. Rather than shy away from those realities, the filmmakers embraced them. Related Stories Movies The Underdog Story Behind the Underdog Story Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Powers $31M in Historic Box Office Launch Against Subdued 'Cat in the Hat'

“We very much wanted to show the city as it was from the viewpoint of Rocky, from the viewpoint of a working-class guy,” producer Irwin Winkler said.

From the rowhouses and neighborhood streets of South Philadelphia to the modest pet shop where Adrian worked, Rocky captured a community of ordinary people trying to make ends meet. Rocky collected debts for a loan shark, Adrian struggled with her confidence, and Paulie was rough around the edges, but beneath their imperfections were characters whose humanity made them relatable, Winkler recalled.

One of the film’s most enduring images wasn’t even part of the original screenplay, according to I Play Rocky director Peter Farrelly .

With the production operating on a limited budget, the filmmakers relied heavily on the newly developed Steadicam , invented the year prior by cinematographer Garrett Brown . The Steadicam allowed filmmakers to follow moving subjects with unprecedented freedom, and Rocky director John G. Avildsen recruited Brown to operate his new invention for the now iconic “Rocky Steps” sequence. The result transformed a simple training run into a universal image of triumph, with Rocky reaching the top of the steps and raising his arms toward the Philadelphia skyline.

entertainment.title: American Idol Reveals 'Major Changes' For Season 25, Including No More Hollywood Week — Here's Why
entertainment.summary: American Idol is saying goodbye to Hollywood (in more ways than one) in Season 25. Here's everything you need to know before the show returns in February.
entertainment.body:
ABC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "American Idol" is dimming the lights on one of its time-honored traditions, officially doing away with Hollywood Week for the show's upcoming Season 25, TVLine has learned.

Historically, contestants who received a Golden Ticket during their auditions would then proceed to Hollywood Week, hence the judges telling them, "You're going to Hollywood!" Season 24 relocated Hollywood Week to Nashville , which was apparently the first step in "Idol" getting rid of it entirely.

"Going to America's Vote is what this show is about," showrunner Megan Michaels Wolflick tells Deadline , explaining that "Hollywood was a metaphor. ... The auditions and the live shows are the bread and butter for this show, and the process of a Hollywood Week is really a culling process that we were televising."

This is just part of what Wolflick calls a "major departure" from the show's previous format, promising "major changes coming" to the long-running singing competition show.

So, how will the show work now? Season 25 will consist of just three audition episodes, as opposed to the usual four (or sometimes five). From those auditions, 25 contestants will receive Golden Tickets from the judges, and those contestants will then compete in a two-episode showdown at Disney's Aulani Resort in Hawaii.

But not all is lost for the contestants who don't receive Golden Tickets during their auditions. Three "standout hopefuls" who don't snag a ticket will be presented to fans on social media, and one of them will be voted in to join the other 25 contestants in Hawaii.

That will mark the end of the season's pre-recorded episodes. From that point on, Season 25 will be going live, putting the contestants at the mercy of viewers' votes much earlier in the season than normal.

ABC And those aren't the only "major changes" coming to "American Idol" in Season 25. The live episodes, which were previously filmed in Los Angeles, will take place at Trilith Live in Atlanta, Georgia, thus ending the show's long-standing ties to Hollywood.

entertainment.title: Bruce Springsteen’s Historic 1988 East Berlin Concert Chronicled in New Documentary
entertainment.summary: When The Walls Came Down features new interviews with Springsteen, Jon Landau, and the E Street Band about their legendary Cold War-era gig in Germany
entertainment.body:
On July 19th, 1988, Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band performed to an estimated crowd of 300,000 fans in East Berlin, just a few miles from the Berlin Wall that had divided the city in half for decades. “I want to tell you that I’m not here for or against any government,” he said to the crowd in prepared remarks that he delivered in German. “I have come to play rock & roll for the East-Berliners in the hope that one day all barriers will be torn down.” Just over a year later, the Berlin Wall fell.

The story of this incredible concert will be told in the upcoming documentary When The Walls Came Down , directed by Nicholas de Taranto and Danielle Peck and featuring new interviews with Springsteen, Jon Landau, Roy Bittan, Patti Scialfa, Stevie Van Zandt, and Max Weinberg. There are also conversations with former East Germans who attended the show, unseen archival footage, and unsealed Stasi files about the band.

“When Bruce and I discussed playing in Communist East Berlin in 1988, we knew it would have impact,” Landau said in a statement. “But it was only when we arrived at Radrennbahn Weissensee, saw the 300,000 fans thirsting for music, connection, and most of all, freedom, that we realized this was going to be one concert that would stay in our hearts — and the hearts of every single person who was there — forever. When the Walls Came Down tells the beautiful and emotional story of that day with complete integrity and accuracy.”

entertainment.title: The Sammy Kershaw Kerfuffle: How Red Carpets Work, And How They Could Change
entertainment.summary: In this week's Billboard Country Update lead story, we talk to experts about what it's like on the red carpet.
entertainment.body:
When the Country Music Association presents its 60th annual awards on Nov. 18, nine-time nominee Ella Langley , seven-timer Miranda Lambert and five-timer Kacey Musgraves all have the potential for a big night. Explore Ella Langley Kacey Musgraves Miranda Lambert See latest videos, charts and news

Who seemed to get the most attention in the run-up to the awards?

So far, that would be Sammy Kershaw, an artist who hasn’t had a top 10 single in 28 years and has just one CMA nomination — a 1993 nod for the Horizon award — in his history. In a single social-media post on Nov. 6, less than two weeks before the awards, he lamented that he’d been “strung along for months,” only to discover that he would not be allowed to walk the red carpet. The Kershaw kerfuffle generated criticism from the general public, which mostly perceived the decision as a slight to an older artist. Rodney Atkins, Stella Parton and The Frontmen Live — Tim Rushlow, Larry Stewart and Richie McDonald — subsequently revealed similar interactions with the CMA, and artists such as Riley Green, Clay Walker, Pam Tillis and Jake Owen voiced support and/or sympathy for Kershaw. Related Noah Kahan Reacts to 2027 Grammy Nominations Snub: 'I Was In My Feelings for a Sec' 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Revs Its Engines & Leads 2026 Game Awards Nominations: Full List Cody Johnson on Why He's Skipping 2026 CMA Awards: 'Going 100 MPH All the Time Isn't Healthy'

The drama placed the trade organization in a tough position. It’s in the CMA’s best interest to have a positive relationship with every artist in the genre, and it’s generally accepted that the trade organization will never say anything negative about any performer. But the carpet — as glamorous as it might appear on a TV at home — is actually a high-stress, high-priced work environment that’s utterly chaotic, no matter how much effort goes into planning. Even if the CMA wanted to accommodate him, Kershaw represents just one member in a class of artists that’s problematic for some other red-carpet participants, all of whom use the carpet for different purposes.

While plenty of fans have seen red-carpet coverage on TV, most consumers — and, probably, the majority of the industry itself — have never actually experienced one in person. Carpets involve three different camps: the awards show; the artists, along with their teams; and the media. For a balanced understanding of the controversy, the Billboard Country Update talked with two people who have worked in two of those three areas: Triple 8 manager Scott Stem, a former CMA publicist who now manages Scotty McCreery; and TriStar Southern Hills Medical Center director of communications Jesse Knutson, who previously covered red carpets as a reporter for WTVF-TV Nashville and organized them as an Academy of Country Music publicist.

entertainment.title: Luminate Adds Songwriter and Publishing Information to Service
entertainment.summary: Available for an additional fee, Luminate now allows users to dig into songwriter and publisher information, thanks to new partnerships with CISAC and the MLC.
entertainment.body:
Entertainment data platform Luminate has added music publishing and songwriter data to its CONNECT service, starting Wednesday (Nov. 18). Available for an additional fee, Luminate users can now see the information and activity attached to musical works as well as recordings on the platform for the first time.

Over time, Luminate plans to track publishing rights to musical works and display which songwriters and publishers control those rights on their dashboards.

According to the blog post, written by Luminate’s chief product officer Arnaud Retureau , there are several expected benefits of its new publishing data: music publishers can “see how every version of a work is performing worldwide,” investors can “get a clearer foundation for forecasting a catalog’s value over time,” performing rights organizations (PROs) can better “monitor their registered ISWCs for future royalty payments,” labels and distributors can “clean up metadata” and “check release readiness” and streaming services can get a clearer view of publishing rights.

Providing transparency about publishing data has long been a challenge in the music business. Often, songs — also called “musical works” — are written by several songwriters, all of whom are represented by music publishers. Given the song is owned by a complex web of rights holders, it’s much more common to find clerical errors in publishing registrations than it is on the recorded music side. To make the system even worse, sometimes recordings are released on streaming services without the songwriters finalizing the arrangement of who owns what part of the publishing, leading to even more issues within the system.

The news comes just months after Luminate announced its plans to add labels to AI music on its service. Set to launch later this year, the company aims to identify these AI works with a combination of its own identification system, data from streaming services and information from the AI music companies themselves.

If protest songs require a ready audience, Jesse Welles certainly had a hungry one on his episode of Austin City Limits , set to air in February. The “War Isn’t Murder” singer made his ACL debut with an hour-long set featuring hits from his now-Grammy nominated album Masks Off . This included a high-octane performance of Black Sabbath’s iconic “War Pigs” as well as his record’s titular song for the Feb. 13 special, which is premiering exclusively on Rolling Stone .

The performance took place under a set of cascading powerlines, a nod to his track-heavy compilations Under the Powerlines , and included nods to the political nature of Welles’ most popular work — like the rough shape of the U.S. Capitol Building in the background. “In the fields, the bodies burning / As the war machine keeps turning,” Welles crooned to synchronized electric guitars. “Death and hatred to mankind / Poisoning their brainwashed minds / Oh, Lord, yeah!”

Welles also blasted out his anti-MAGA folk rock anthem “Masks Off,” just one in his stacked lineup of Americana -focused protest songs including “War Isn’t Murder” and “The Nerd Reich.” “Killing people from a distance in an instant / At the insistence of a president / With a blackmail gun to his head / For the fun that he had in the Dark Ages / Pages and pages and pages and pages / They thought they’d get away with it,” he sang before landing the song’s deceptively simple chorus. “All the masks are off / And they’re getting lazy / They think you’re so damn stupid / They think you’re so damn crazy.”

News of the special comes days after Welles was nominated five times at 2027 Grammys, for Best American Roots Song, Best Americana Album, Best American Roots Performance, Best Americana Performance, and Best Traditional Folk Album. It’s the second nomination year for Welles, who started as a viral sensation on TikTok before getting the stamp of approval from massive voices in the folk and Americana scene like Joan Baez, Dave Matthews, Nathaniel Rateliff, and Margo Price.

entertainment.body:
The BMI Country Awards honored the songwriters and publishers behind many of the year’s biggest country hits on Tuesday (Nov. 17). Held at BMI’s Nashville offices, the annual celebration was what BMI’s CEO Mike O’Neill called “the biggest parking lot party in Nashville.” Explore Ella Langley Jeffrey Steele Miranda Lambert See latest videos, charts and news

“You all give us the words we can’t find on our own,” he said to the songwriters in the room. Related Noah Kahan Reacts to 2027 Grammy Nominations Snub: 'I Was In My Feelings for a Sec' 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Revs Its Engines & Leads 2026 Game Awards Nominations: Full List Cody Johnson on Why He's Skipping 2026 CMA Awards: 'Going 100 MPH All the Time Isn't Healthy'

To honor the massive, genre-shifting success of “Choosin’ Texas” — written by Ella Langley, Luke Dick, Miranda Lambert and Joybeth Taylor, and recorded by Langley — the BMI Country Awards presented the writers with the inaugural BMI Impact Award, which recognizes a song, songwriter or artist whose cultural impact has distinguished their creative work as a defining force. “Choosin’ Texas” has spent 28 weeks atop the all-genre Billboard Hot 100 so far, holding the all-time record for the most weeks at No. 1 on that chart. To honor the writers, Thomas Rhett took the stage to perform “Choosin’ Texas.”

Morgan Wallen and Charlie Handsome were both named BMI country songwriter of the year for cowriting seven of BMI’s most performed country songs of the year, among them “I Ain’t Comin’ Back,” “I Got Better,” “Superman” and “I’m the Problem.”

Handsome took the stage and praised Wallen for his win. “He’s one of the best songwriters I’ve ever met and he deserves recognition … he’s a great songwriter and artist,” he said.

“I’m the Problem” was named the 2026 BMI country song of the year and is published by Big Loud Mountain, Bo Jewell Club, Ernest Money Music, Honey Hole Publishing, Sony/ATV Songs LLC and Warner-Tamerlane Publishing Corp. The song was written by Grady Block, Handsome, Jamie McLaughlin, Ernest Keith Smith and Wallen. “I’m the Problem” topped the Country Airplay chart for eight weeks, making it one of only six songs in the chart’s history since 1990 to stay at the pinnacle for eight or more weeks.

Warner-Tamerlane Publishing Corp. took home publisher of the year. In the past year, the company published 31 of the most performed songs, among them “20 Cigarettes,” “I’m the Problem,” “Single Again” and “After All the Bars Are Closed.”

sports.title: The early reviews for the Madden movie aren't good
sports.summary: The Madden movie, starring Nicolas Cage as the legendary coach, broadcaster, and video-game mogul, has landed on Prime Video.
sports.body:
The current consensus at Rotten Tomatoes, based on 16 reviews, is 13 percent .

The folks at Sports Business Journal have collected and summarized some of the feedback. Owen Gleiberman of Variety calls it a “stunt biopic on cinematic amphetamines,” adding that “ it’s like an SNL sketch shot and edited by Scorsese .”

Then there’s this incredible lede from David Rooney of the Hollywood Reporter : “Imagine being cornered at a party while sober by a wired cokehead determined to tell you a long, painstakingly detailed story without pausing for breath and you might have some idea of the exhausting experience of watching Madden .”

Bryan Curtis of The Ringer says "[i]t’s not quite as awful as the trailers made it look,” but that it still “isn’t good.” Curtis also says Christian Bale is “mesmerizing” as Al Davis, which raises the question of why they didn’t just make an Al Davis movie?

Of course, I’ll still watch it. You should, too. But I have a feeling that, throughout the experience, I’ll be wondering how much John Madden himself would have hated it.

Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Wednesday that getting flexed is “really cool for our players.”

“I said it at the beginning of the year. I mean, you want to be on Thursday Night, Sunday Night, Monday Night — you want to be flexed, means you’re having a good year,” Monken said, via transcript from the team. “As nice as it is to have a one o’clock schedule every week, I mean, I said that, early in the [year]. I mean, you’re on a trajectory to be fired at some point because you’re at one o’clock every week. So, you’re fighting like hell to get to where you’re on national TV. So, if people are going to watch football, and more importantly than that, an opportunity to get to seven [wins].”

Monken also agreed that it’s a good test for the Browns as a young team.

“I think you earn where you’re at in the present moment, and that only lends itself to what’s in front of you and how important that’s going to become,” Monken said. “You know, getting the bye at 6-4 and putting yourself in position where the rest of the games matter, and especially the one coming up.”

This will be the Browns’ first Sunday night game at home since 2019, which should make for a rowdy atmosphere on the shores of Lake Erie.

“Oh, it’s a huge advantage. Huge advantage,” Monken said of the anticipated environment. “Making it hard for the opposing offense, cadence-wise, being able to function, and making an advantage for us when we’re on offense. I mean, it’s a huge advantage, and it should be playing at home.”

sports.title: No practice for Baker Mayfield on Wednesday
sports.summary: Word on Tuesday was that Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield's outlook for this week's game against the Lions was not promising and Wednesday didn't bring any better news.
sports.body:
Mayfield is dealing with a foot injury that had him in a walking boot during the team’s bye week and he watched practice in street clothes on Wednesday. The Buccaneers have not made any official determination of his status, but things appear to be trending in the wrong direction.

Jalon Daniels will make his fourth start of the season if Mayfield is unable to play this weekend. The Bucs added Easton Stick to the roster as a third quarterback this week.

Reporters at the open portion of practice also noted that safety Antoine Winfield was not taking part for Tampa.

sports.title: Tory Horton's heads up play earns him NFC special teams player of the week
sports.summary: Late in Sunday's victory over the Raiders, Seahawks receiver Tory Horton made a heads-up play on special teams that helped seal the win.
sports.body:
The league has recognized Horton for his efforts, naming him special teams player of the week.

There was 2:04 remaining in the fourth quarter after Las Vegas narrowed Seattle’s lead to one possession with a 43-yard field goal. The Raiders tried to send the kickoff out of the end zone to preserve the two-minute warning, having just two timeouts left. But Horton leapt up and tipped the ball into the end zone to prevent a touchback. He then signaled for Rashid Shaheed to pick up the football, as he’d stepped out of bounds, to prevent an illegal touch.

Shaheed returned the ball 22 yards, taking the clock down to 1:59.

While the play was flagged for an illegal bat, Las Vegas declined it. A re-kick would have taken more time off the clock.

Quarterback Drew Lock then sealed the victory with a 15-yard run.

sports.title: Cam Little is AFC special teams player of the week for second week in a row
sports.summary: Jaguars kicker Cam Little turned in another strong game against the Titans last Sunday.
sports.body:
Little made all four field goals and all four extra points he attempted in Jacksonville’s 40-23 win. It was the second straight week that Little made four field goals and the NFL recognized his accomplishment both times.

Little was named the AFC special teams player of the week for the second week in a row. It’s the first time that’s happened since Cameron Dicker in 2024 and Little joins punter Bryan Barker as the only Jaguars players to pull off the double.

Little is now 18-of-20 on field goals and 29-of-30 on extra points for the season.

sports.title: Colts CB Justin Walley named the AFC defensive player of the week
sports.summary: The Colts ended a five-game losing streak with last Sunday's win over the Dolphins and a defensive touchdown played a big role in the 24-22 win.
sports.body:
Cornerback Justin Walley got home on a blitz deep inside Miami territory and separated Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord from the ball. Defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore recovered the ball for a touchdown.

Walley had five tackles, two tackles for loss and two passes defensed overall in the win. The third-round pick has 40 tackles, two sacks and three forced fumbles to this point in his rookie season.

The NFL named Walley the AFC defensive player of the week on Wednesday. It’s the first time a Colt has won the award since early in the 2024 season.

sports.title: Jaelan Phillips wins first NFC defensive player of the week award
sports.summary: The Panthers moved into sole possession of first place in the NFC South with their victory over the Saints on Sunday.
sports.body:
Now one of their players has been recognized for his performance in the win.

Edge rusher Jaelan Phillips has been named NFC defensive player of the week.

Phillips had five total tackles with three for loss, a sack, and a fumble recovery that led to a Panthers touchdown in the 20-17 victory.

According to the league, Phillips is the second player in the conference to have three TFLs and a fumble recovery in a single game in 2026.

This is Phillips’ first career defensive player of the week award.

In his first season with Carolina, Phillips has tallied 3.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, and eight QB hits so far in 2026.

sports.title: Jahmyr Gibbs wins second NFC offensive player of the week award of the season
sports.summary: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs continued his terrific 2026 season in Sunday's win over the Patriots in Munich.
sports.body:
Now the league has recognized him for his performance in that contest.

Gibbs put up 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing, 99 receiving) along with two rushing touchdowns in the 35-10 win.

According to the league, Gibbs is just the second player under the age of 25 in NFL history with at least 250 yards from scrimmage and two rushing touchdowns in multiple games, joining Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson. He also scored his 61st and 62nd touchdowns, which puts him past Hall of Famer Terrell Davis for the most touchdowns by a player in his first four seasons in league history.

The 252 yards were the most by a player in a single game so far this season. They were also the second most in an international game in league history.

Gibbs now has five career offensive player of the week awards. He last won it for Week 5 of this year.

Through nine games, Gibbs leads the league with 1,000 rushing yards, 1,384 yards from scrimmage, 11 rushing touchdowns, and 13 total TDs.

sports.title: Joe Burrow named AFC offensive player of the week for second time this season
sports.summary: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is the betting favorite to be the NFL MVP this season and games like the one he had last Sunday are the reason why he's in that spot.
sports.body:
Burrow lit up the Steelers during a 38-18 win that extended Cincinnati’s winning streak to five games. Burrow was 35-of-44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the victory.

The four touchdowns moved him up to 20 over the course of the winning streak and he leads the league with 27 touchdown passes over the entire season.

The NFL announced on Wednesday that Burrow has been named the AFC offensive player of the week. It’s the second time he’s won that prize this season and the 10th time in his career.

sports.title: Geno Smith will be limited in Wednesday's practice
sports.summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith avoided a major ankle injury in last Sunday's loss to the Bills, but his Week 11 status remains uncertain.
sports.body:
Head coach Aaron Glenn said at his press conference that Smith will be a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice as the team works to get ready to face the Chargers. Glenn said that the team will see how the week plays out before making any determination about Smith’s availability for the game.

Fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut against the Bills and will make his first pro start if Smith is unable to play.

Wide receivers Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) will not practice on Wednesday due to injuries suffered in Week 10.

sports.title: Ben Johnson sees Bears' 4.2 yards per carry average as "a deceiving statistic"
sports.summary: League wide, NFL teams average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt.
sports.body:
What Johnson does care about is that the running game is efficient, and Johnson would like to see better efficiency than he has seen so far from his offense. Johnson noted that an occasional long run can skew the yards per carry average, and if there are too many runs getting stuffed for no gain, that’s a problem. On the flip side, a one-yard run will bring down any team’s average, but it’s a great play if it happens on fourth-and-goal at the 1-yard line.

“I don’t see it as bigger chunk runs, necessarily. The yards per carry is a deceiving statistic in a lot of ways,” Johnson said. “We run the ball a lot in the red zone, and when you’re down there a four-yard carry is really an explosive.”

Johnson said what he cares more about is efficiency. Many teams look at running success rate, which means the percentage of runs on which a team gains at least 40 percent of yardage needed on first down, at least 60 percent on second down, or at least 100 percent on third or fourth down. The Bears’ success rate this season is 49.2 percent, and Johnson says that’s not good enough.

“We go off efficiency, and we’re under 50 percent efficient running the ball. We set our bar higher than that. We want to be closer to 55 percent, so we’ve got some work to do and all our guys know it,” Johnson said.

Ultimately, Johnson wants to see rushing first downs and rushing touchdowns. Yards per carry is secondary to that.

sports.title: 49ers likely won't cut Brandon Aiyuk until they have to
sports.summary: With a roster exemption that lasts until November 24 and with no requirement to pay him a penny until the exemption expires, the 49ers have shown no inclination to release receiver Brandon Aiyuk until they absolutely have to.
sports.body:
Nine days since Aiyuk was reinstated from the reserve/left squad list, the 49ers haven’t cut him. At this point, with only six days to go, the 49ers surely will kick the can as long as they can.

They gain nothing from delaying Aiyuk’s return, other than the relatively minor strategic advantage of keeping him away from a competitor. With all signs pointing to Aiyuk landing in Washington, he’s no threat to San Francisco’s playoff interests.

Of course, the receiver-needy Rams could get involved. Or perhaps the Vikings, who are currently without Jordan Addison. Or maybe the Seahawks, who don’t have a clear No. 2 option behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

If the 49ers are simply squatting on Aiyuk out of spite, that’s a bush-league move that creates bad karma. Let the guy get back in the league. They apparently still have the ability to pursue upwards of $13 million in bonus money from him; use that process as the vehicle for getting a pound of flesh.

Regardless, the 49ers apparently won’t be letting him go until the exemption expires. At that point, he’ll pass through waivers, his contract won’t be claimed, and he’ll become a free agent.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills have loved running the football thus far in the 2026 season. James Cook has the second-most carries in the NFL right now at 187. As a team, the Bills are the current owners of the second-highest first-down designed run rate in the NFL at 61.3%. Now, sure, the Bills have recently played in a collection of games that featured plenty of garbage time, when Buffalo has attempted to burn clock by tapping into the run game. Even when garbage-time is considered, the Bills have the NFL’s second-highest run rate on all downs at 45.7%. The rest of the league averages a designed run play on 39.3%. Quarterback scrambles — that occur on dropbacks — and spikes and kneels are excluded in that calculation. Analytics have proven that passing the football is more efficient than running the football. And this article isn’t going to show that the Bills have actually become more efficient on the ground than through the air. Right now, in non-garbage time situations, Buffalo’s designed-run game has provided the team +0.023 EPA per play, the eighth-highest figure in the NFL. The team’s pass game has provided the team +0.239 EPA per dropback, the fourth-best in football. Unsurprisingly, the difference in value added for each method of moving the football has been seismic. Up until now, the Bills have genuinely attempted to “establish” the run in their first nine games of the 2026 campaign. sports.title: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings prepare to face his former team
sports.summary: Sunday night's game in Mexico City between the Vikings and 49ers has multiple interesting subplots.
sports.body:
Jauan Jennings is in his first season as a Viking. In six games with two starts, he has only six catches for 54 yards.

And there was a strong possibility of a trade back to the 49ers. He ultimately decided to stay where he was .

The Vikings will need him on Sunday night, especially with receiver Jordan Addison out due to a thumb injury.

“With us being down Jordan Addison, we’re gonna need him to make some plays in the pass game ,” coach Kevin O’Connell said Tuesday on KFAN.

Jennings didn’t play in Week 10 at Green Bay due to a calf injury.

During five seasons with the 49ers, Jennings caught 210 passes for 2,581 yards and 22 touchdowns in 75 regular-season games. He also had 23 catches for 289 yards and a touchdown in 11 postseason games — including four catches for 42 yards and a touchdown and a touchdown pass in Super Bowl LIX.

Without Addison, Jennings could get more opportunities. And he will surely have a little extra incentive to show his former team that they should have kept him around.

sports.title: Report: Jaguars C Robert Hainsey week-to-week with knee injury
sports.summary: Jaguars center Robert Hainsey left last Sunday's win over the Titans with a knee injury and it looks like he will need some more time to recover.
sports.body:
Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that Hainsey is dealing with a sprain and is considered week-to-week when it comes to a return to action. While Hainsey is set to miss time, he is not expected to be out through the rest of the regular season.

sports.title: Report: Mike Pettine takes over as Cowboys' defensive play-caller
sports.summary: Christian Parker will remain the defensive coordinator.
sports.body:
Via ESPN, Pettine will be taking over as the play-caller for the Dallas Cowboys defense.

Pettine supplants defensive coordinator Christian Parker, a Pettine protege who is in his first year as the coach in charge of an NFL defense. Parker will remain the team’s defensive coordinator.

It was obvious that something was coming. Sunday’s 46-40 loss to the 49ers included an embarrassing performance from the defense, highlighted by multiple players running the wrong way when receiver Deebo Samuel rumbled 70 yards for a rushing touchdown.

Some would say Pettine is part of the problem, given that he has been there for multiple weeks. Short of firing everyone and hiring someone off the street, however, there’s not much that can be done right now.

The first test comes on Sunday, when the Cowboys host the one-win Titans. Four days later, Dallas faces the two-win Eagles. If the Cowboys don’t win both, they’ll likely be de facto done for 2026.

sports.title: C.J. Stroud: "There's still a lot of ball to be played"
sports.summary: With Sunday's loss to the Browns, the Texans have fallen to 3-6 on the season.
sports.body:
At this point, Houston will have to rip off several wins in a row to have a chance at the postseason.

“There’s still a lot of ball to be played, if I can remember I think we’ll be fine,” Stroud said on Tuesday, via transcript from the team. “It’s not perfection that is what’s needed, but it’s a chase of excellence from everybody. Me and [ Will Anderson Jr.], we try to set the standard every day for everybody in the building to look at us and be like, ‘Hey, those are two guys that I want to follow after,’ and it’s up to us to keep that standard going.

“It doesn’t mean because you lose a couple games that everything got to switch or change. There’s a lot of ball to be played left, so we’re still excited about what’s coming next.”

So Stroud remains motivated and wants that attitude to permeate throughout the team.

“What else are we going to do? Cry about it and hold our heads down? Woe is us, woe is this team? I don’t believe in that,” Stroud said. “It sucks, yeah, I’m not the happiest camper, but I think the motivated me is one of the best me’s that I’ve seen.

“I think even as this team, the motivated Texans is a scary team. It’s up to us. We don’t need anybody else. That’s my message to the guys. We don’t need anybody else to have faith in us or to think that we can do this or can’t do this. It doesn’t really matter. We’re the ones on the field making plays and we have the opportunity. Everybody can have an opinion, but when you have the opportunity, you’ve got to go and do it and I think it just starts one thing at a time.”

sports.title: Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla: "We’re very happy with both the team and the location right now"
sports.summary: A pattern has emerged during the early months of Vinod Khosla's ownership of the Seahawks.
sports.body:
First, he’ll make a less-than-unequivocal comment about the future of the team in Seattle. Two, people will hear his words and repeat them. Three, he will complain about that.

Most recently, Khosla was asked directly during an appearance on CNBC whether he’d consider moving the team.

“I’ve not made any plans or even discussed -- I know the press like to make a big deal of it,” Khosla said, via Sports Business Journal . “We’re very happy with both the team and the location right now.”

And there it is. “Right now.” Why add “right now”? Just end the sentence at “location.”

The same thing happened last month, when Khosla was interviewed by Axios . Asked point-blank whether he’d make a commitment to keeping the Seahawks in Seattle over the long term, Khosla said, “ I will never say never . Will this team be in Seattle 500 years from now? But I have no current plans to change anything about the team, including the coach, president, operation or Lumen Field. It all functions well.”

It’s not difficult (although apparently it is). The question is simple. Will you move from Seattle?

While there’s an element of taxpayer-funding leverage that arises regarding future stadium renovations and/or construction in Seattle, there’s a way to answer the question that doesn’t sacrifice future bargaining power.

“We have every intention to remain in Seattle” is the easiest reply. With no further elaboration or explanation.

sports.title: Gardner Minshew had surgery to repair torn ligament in throwing elbow
sports.summary: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew has had surgery to repair the elbow injury that ended his season.
sports.body:
Minshew had the surgery on his right ulnar collateral ligament on Monday and is expected to make a full recovery , according to ESPN.

Although tearing the UCL is a famously brutal injury for baseball pitchers that necessitated the development of the Tommy John surgery procedure, it tends not to be as severe for the throwing motion of a quarterback. Brock Purdy tore his UCL in the 49ers’ playoff loss in January of 2023, had surgery to repair it in March, and was healthy enough to play the full season and lead the 49ers to the Super Bowl the next year.

Minshew, who will be a free agent in March, should be healthy enough to sign with some team and play in 2027. Where he’ll be playing remains a question.

sports.title: When Brian Flores defenses face Kyle Shanahan offenses, Flores is 5-0
sports.summary: Teams with Flores as a head coach or defensive assistant have played against teams with Shanahan as a head coach or offensive assistant five times, and Flores is 5-0.
sports.body:
Teams with Flores as a head coach or defensive assistant have played against teams with Shanahan as a head coach or offensive assistant five times, and Flores is 5-0.

Since becoming defensive coordinator of the Vikings, Flores has coached against Shanahan’s 49ers twice, with Flores’ team coming out on top both times. In 2023, the Vikings beat the 49ers 22-17. In 2024, the Vikings beat the 49ers 23-17.

Flores and Shanahan coached against each other as head coaches once, in 2020, when Flores’ Dolphins beat Shanahan’s 49ers 43-17.

The most famous game with Flores and Shanahan on opposite sides came in Super Bowl LI, when Flores was linebackers coach for the Patriots and Shanahan was offensive coordinator for the Falcons. Shanahan’s Falcons jumped out to a 28-3 lead, only to have Flores’ Patriots come back and win 34-28 in overtime.

And in 2011, New England beat Washington 34-27 when Flores was a defensive assistant in New England and Shanahan was offensive coordinator in Washington.

Shanahan was once on a coaching staff that got a win against a team with Flores on the staff, in the final game of the 2009 season, when the Patriots had already clinched their playoff spot, rested starters and lost to a Texans team with Shanahan as offensive coordinator. But Flores was a special teams assistant, not a defensive assistant, on that Patriots team, so that game wasn’t a Flores defense vs. Shanahan offense competition.

When it’s Flores coaching defense against Shanahan coaching offense, the result has been the same across different teams and in different coaching roles: Flores has five wins and Shanahan has none.

sports.body: Sometimes, important additions to an NFL team don’t occur until close to September… or even in-season. On August 18, after their first preseason game, the Bills signed veteran defensive lineman Greg Gaines — potentially as a response to rookie defensive tackle Zane Durant being injured late in the opening exhibition game against the Panthers. Almost exactly two weeks later, on the last day of August, as the team seemingly had no clear-cut candidate to return punts, Buffalo scooped up Greg Dortch after he was surprisingly cut by the Lions. Through the first nine games of the season, both have provided valuable, low-key contributions to this Bills team. On the surface, Gaines’ presence has been irrelevant. He has 11 tackles and one tackles for loss along with two pressures on 77 pass-rush snaps on 22.5% of Buffalo’s defensive snaps. But when Gaines is on the field, he’s a magnet for blockers, which has a massive ripple effect on his teammates. More blockers on him, fewer on other Bills defenders. Gaines is currently 10th in the NFL among qualifying defensive linemen in double-team rate (67.5%) on pass-rush snaps. It’s the highest rate on Buffalo’s roster right now (among qualifiers). As for Dortch, the value he’s added has been easier to discern. Among punt returners with at least 15 returns to date, his 9.2 yards-per-return average is seventh-best in the NFL. He’s been darn good as a kicker returner too, so teams aren’t able to simply directionally kick it away from reigning All-Pro kicker returner Ray Davis. While Davis is second in the NFL in average kick-return yardage at 29.6 entering Week 11, Dortch is tied for 12th with an average of 27.2 yards per kick return. And he’s actually returned nearly double the amount of kickoffs (23) as Davis (12). And then there’s Amani Hooker. Of course, the jury is still out on how much the trade-deadline acquisition will impact Buffalo’s defense. But in his first game, after a week of practice in a new scheme on a new team, he played the most defensive snaps of any Bills defender (70), made seven tackles, and had a pass breakup that was nearly an interception. Hooker will play a full-time role at free safety the rest of the way. Gaines and Dortch have proven to be savvy, low-cost additions by the Bills close to the start of the regular season. sports.body: The New York Jets have solicited advice from nearly everyone on planet Earth when hiring head coaches this century. That has included The 33rd Team, Charley Casserly, and do you remember that one time when Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning made a phone call to seal the deal for Adam Gase? Great times. That can’t happen in 2027. Make no mistake about it: the Jets will be looking for a new head coach in a matter of months, but in all of those other situations, they lost the battle before it ever began. Gibbs has touched the ball an NFL-high 240 times this season, combining 199 carries and 41 catches. With that kind of workload, the biggest concern for the Lions will be whether he can stay healthy for 17 regular-season games and, the Lions hope, some playoff games after that.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills announced a series of roster moves as they begin preparations to host the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium for Week 11. Buffalo has signed defensive back Te’Cory Couch to the practice squad, bringing him back to One Bills Drive after being released ahead of last weekend’s game and once he cleared waivers Monday afternoon. Couch joined the Bills in 2024, entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie free agent. To make room for Couch, Buffalo once again parted ways with veteran offensive guard Nick Broeker, who has been re-added to the team’s practice squad several times already this season. Broeker has yet to appear in a regular-season game for the Bills, though he has previously played in 12 games (2023 and 2024 seasons) for the Denver Broncos. Broeker was originally drafted by Buffalo in Round 7 (230th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft. The Bills also announced that rookie offensive guard Ar’maj Reed-Adams has been placed on Injured Reserve, which will sideline him for at least the next four games. With Reed-Adams heading to IR, that opens up a spot on Buffalo’s 53-man roster. But Drew Lock has made it reasonable to question whether Darnold should get benched.

That’s because Lock has played three full games, and most of a fourth, while Darnold has missed time with injuries this season. And Lock hasn’t just been better than Darnold. Lock has been so much better that there’s no comparison between the two.

The Seahawks are 4-0 in the games when Lock was their primary quarterback. They’re 2-4 in the games with Darnold as the primary quarterback.

Of the 37 NFL quarterbacks who have thrown at least 90 passes this season, Lock ranks first with a passer rating of 125.6. Darnold ranks 31st with a passer rating of 79.5.

Lock has still not thrown an interception this season. Darnold has thrown nine.

sports.title: Brian Flores: Vikings plan to rotate players in order to deal with altitude in Mexico City
sports.summary: The 49ers are spending the week in Colorado in order to acclimate to the altitude at which their Week 11 game in Mexico City will be played.
sports.body:
But the Vikings have a plan for ensuring that their players are ready for the conditions.

“It’s a tough place to play,” Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores told reporters on Tuesday regarding the game in Mexico. “I think it’s certainly taxing, you know, I think you’re — I think as a staff, we’re already talking about, ‘Hey, we’re gonna have to rotate these guys and get, you know, everybody’s gonna have to be ready to play.’ And so, yeah, I mean, it’s certainly something that we’re going to have to deal with.

“But there’s always, you know, elements that we’re dealing with, whether it’s cold or rain or things like that. Obviously, we’re indoors, so we don’t deal with much of that. But that’s the environment we’re gonna be in. I think we prepare them to play in that environment, but I’m not gonna be silly and say, ‘Hey, everybody, hey, you’ve got to go in there for 12 straight plays.’ I mean, we’re not doing that.

“So we’ll have rotations, we’ll have a plan in place. Inevitably, we’re gonna have to fight through some of that. It’s not gonna be your average game where, you know, altitude, you just have — you literally have less oxygen. So we’ve got to do a great job as a staff of making sure — watching guys, and making sure we got guys in and out, you know, as much as we can.”

His broader message to the defense is clear: “We’re gonna need everybody.”

Regardless of the plan to rotate players, the question becomes whether the 49ers will be able to rely more heavily on their best players because they’re properly acclimated to the thinner air. The Vikings are choosing a different strategy, and it’s going to create an obvious apples to apples comparison between the approaches that the two teams have taken — especially if the 49ers players seem to be fresh and the Vikings players seem to be gassed.

In the first six games of the 2026 season, wh
sports.body: Yes, the Buffalo Bills have gone from a gauntlet of high-level quarterbacks to start to the season to a consecutive collection of backups, and that drastic shift in competition has coincided with a drastic shift in defensive philosophy from Jim Leonhard. In the first six games of the 2026 season, when Buffalo’s defense was a liability, the Bills played man coverage 16.4% of the time, per Fantasy Points Data. That was the 24th-highest man-coverage rate in the NFL. Also in those first six outings, Buffalo’s blitz rate was 27.9%, the 20th-highest blitz rate in football. Then the bye week happened. Since then, the Bills’ man-coverage rate jumped to 25.7%. In that three-game sample, that’s the 13th-highest in the league. Buffalo’s blitz rate has been 33.6% combined in Weeks 8, 9, and 10, the 13th-highest blitz rate in the NFL. (Can’t forget too — there was plenty of garbage time in all three contests, where the Bills, like any team, were prompted to sit back in soft zone to keep everything in front of them.) The new man-coverage and blitz rates don’t represent massive, 180-degree changes in philosophy. And we likely won’t be able to fully discern how much Leonhard’s man-coverage and blitzing movement post-bye has actually made the Bills defense better until Thanksgiving night against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. But one thing is for sure — Leonhard’s defense has recently started to look like what we expected Leonhard’s defense to look like all along.

sports.title: Dan Campbell: I'm not telling players to stop celebrating because of Aidan Hutchinson's injury
sports.summary: Hutchinson tore his ACL while celebrating a sack.
sports.body:
Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season after injuring his right knee while celebrating a sack of Drake Maye in Sunday’s game. Hutchinson jumped in the air and immediately grabbed his right knee after suffering the injury when he landed back on the turf in Munich.

“I hate it, I know he hates it. But I mean, the number of moves that I’ve seen Hutch make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one leg lateral movements, lateral balances, I’m just like, it was one of those things, man,” Campbell said. “I hate it. The results over these past three weeks (henceforth referred to as “the improvement period”) have been excellent for the Bills defense. The obvious caveat to any discussion here is that the results should be excellent due to the level of play challenging the Buffalo defense, but strong play against backup quarterbacks is certainly preferable to poor play against backup quarterbacks. It’s unquestionably the best stretch of defense the Bills have delivered so far during the regular season, and it comes not just against backup quarterbacks, but also in the three weeks immediately following the Buffalo bye week in Week 7. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports that, while Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season with a torn ACL, he has no other significant damage.

Initial reports indicated the Lions feared Hutchinson “probably” had additional damage in his knee, specifically his meniscus.

Hutchinson and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye were both injured on Hutchinson’s third-down sack of Maye with 9:28 left in the first quarter. Maye injured his ankle on the play, and the injury could be season-ending. Hutchinson injured his knee on the celebration afterward.

Walt Anderson, the NFL’s officiating rules analyst, said through a league spokesman that Hutchinson’s tackle was not an illegal hip drop .

This marks the second time in three seasons that Hutchinson’s season will end early. He finishes 2026 with six sacks.
